Body: `addTeammate` unconditionally pushes `sessionID`, which can create duplicates if the same teammate is added twice (or if a session restarts and re-registers). Consider de-duping the array before writing (and/or storing teammate metadata keyed by session id) to keep status output and broadcasts consistent.

Multiple `JSON.parse(...)` calls are unguarded inside `Effect.gen`. If a file is partially written/corrupted, this will throw synchronously and turn into a defect (especially with `.pipe(Effect.orDie)` on reads), potentially crashing the tool/session. Wrap parsing in `Effect.try` and surface a normal failure (or skip invalid entries with logging).

`addTask` writes directly to `.opencode/teams/{teamID}/tasks/...` without validating that the team exists or ensuring the tasks directory exists. For a wrong/nonexistent `teamID`, this will likely fail as a filesystem error rather than a clear "Team not found" message. Consider checking `getTeam(...)` first and/or using `ensureDir(tasksDir(...))`/`writeWithDirs` for clearer, consistent errors.

`sendMessage` writes directly to `.opencode/teams/{teamID}/messages/...` without validating team existence or ensuring the messages directory exists. A bad `teamID` will surface as a generic filesystem failure (and may `orDie` upstream). Consider checking `getTeam(...)` and ensuring the directory exists (or using `writeWithDirs`) so callers get a clear error.

The description says you must specify the target `session_id`, but the actual parameter name is `to` (and it can also be "*"). Consider aligning the wording with the parameter name (and documenting the "*" broadcast behavior) to avoid confusion for tool callers.

`listTasks` parses each task JSON without guarding against invalid/partial JSON. A single corrupted task file will throw during `JSON.parse` and can defect the whole tool run. Consider wrapping parsing in `Effect.try` and skipping/logging invalid entries so one bad file doesn’t break status for the entire team.

`readMessages` uses `JSON.parse` on every message file without handling parse errors. If a message file is truncated/corrupted, this will throw and can crash message reads. Consider safe parsing with a recoverable failure path (skip invalid messages + log, or return a structured error).

Suggestion for the human to decide: this failure happens after stream parts may already have been persisted on the current assistant message. Because `Effect.retry(...)` wraps the stream before `cleanup()` runs, a retry will start a new stream on the same message without removing the partial text/reasoning parts from the truncated attempt, so a successful retry can leave the original truncated content plus the retried response in the final assistant message. Consider clearing the in-flight attempt parts before retrying, or moving this detection earlier to a place where no partial parts have been committed.

- `text-start` and `reasoning-start` call `session.updatePart(...)` immediately, so partial parts are already in SQLite by the time `finish-step` fires.

The `yield* new MyError(...)` pattern requires `Schema.TaggedErrorClass`-derived errors (Effect's `YieldableError`). `MessageV2.APIError` is built with `namedSchemaError` (`message-v2.ts:51`), which extends `Error` directly without `[Symbol.iterator]`. The suggested form fails to compile:

```
src/session/processor.ts: error TS2488:
  Type 'NamedSchemaError' must have a '[Symbol.iterator]()' method that returns an iterator.
```

All 14 existing `yield* new ...` sites in `src/` use `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` (`UpgradeFailedError`, `CliError`, `PhotonUnavailableError`, `RejectedError`, etc.). Migrating `MessageV2.APIError` and its siblings (`AbortedError`, `OutputLengthError`, `AuthError`, `ContextOverflowError`) from `namedSchemaError` to `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` would change the wire schema (`{ name, data }` → `{ _tag, ... }`) and break SDK consumers — out of scope for this PR.

The tmux DCS passthrough wrapper likely needs an extra ESC (and/or ESC-escaping) before the embedded OSC sequence. With the current template, the payload begins with `ESC ]`, but tmux passthrough commonly expects `ESC`-quoting (resulting in `ESC ESC ]`) so the forwarded output starts with a real `ESC ]`. Please verify against tmux’s passthrough rules and, if needed, either restore the extra `\x1b`/escape ESC bytes in the payload, or drop the leading ESC from `osc52` when embedding so the terminal ultimately receives a valid `ESC ]52...` sequence.

These tests call `copy()`, which always proceeds to `getCopyMethod()` and executes a platform-native clipboard write (spawning `wl-copy`/`xclip`/PowerShell/clipboardy). That makes the test environment-dependent and can introduce flakiness or hangs in CI. Consider testing the OSC52 emission in isolation (e.g., export `writeOsc52`/a pure `buildOsc52Sequence` helper for tests, or stub the native copy method so no external processes run).

`nativeItem` returns early when `entry.role` is set, which means entries that also specify `action` (e.g. zoom items in `DESKTOP_MENU`) will never route through `runDesktopMenuAction`. Because the desktop window disables Electron’s built-in zoom shortcuts via `webContents.on("zoom-changed", ...)`, role-based zoom menu items can end up not working. Consider special-casing zoom roles (reset/zoomIn/zoomOut) to prefer `entry.action` (and use the provided label/accelerator) so menu zoom works reliably.

Menu actions are executed against `BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow()`. If the app has windows but none are focused (e.g. all windows minimized), actions like reload/devtools/close will no-op. Consider falling back to another existing window (e.g. first window, or the same fallback used in `main/index.ts` for `trigger`).

`runDesktopMenuAction` is invoked with `void ...` and no rejection handling. Since this may call `ipcRenderer.invoke(...)`, failures can surface as unhandled promise rejections. Consider attaching a `.catch(() => undefined)` (or routing into your app’s logger) to avoid noisy unhandled rejections.

The trigger button’s `aria-label` is hard-coded ("OpenCode menu"), while the surrounding titlebar uses `useLanguage().t(...)` for aria-labels. Consider localizing this string via `useLanguage()` and adding an i18n key for consistency and accessibility in non-English locales.

`TimelineRowView` now uses a non-null assertion (`timelineRowByKey().get(props.rowKey)!`) and removed the previous `<Show when=... keyed>` guard. If the Virtualizer briefly renders/retains a rowKey that has been removed from `timelineRowByKey()` during reactive updates, this will throw and crash the timeline. Prefer restoring the guard or handling a missing row (e.g., return `null` when the lookup is undefined).

`toolOpen` is stored in a component-level store but is never reset on session changes. If the session route changes without unmounting this component, open-state entries can leak across sessions (and potentially apply to a different session if part IDs collide), and the record can grow unbounded over time. Consider clearing `toolOpen` when `sessionKey()` changes (or scoping the state by sessionKey).

This test logs the full sample set on every run. Unconditional `console.log` output can make CI logs noisy and harder to read; consider removing it or gating it behind an env flag / only logging on failure.

This assertion hard-codes an internal provider naming convention (`custom-openai.responses`), which is likely to be brittle if provider string formatting changes. Prefer asserting on a more stable signal of the chosen API (e.g., a structured field/config indicating Responses API selection), or at least reduce coupling by checking the expected behavior (e.g., provider suffix contains `.responses` and does not contain `.chat`) rather than exact equality.

The persisted disabled ID is removed and written before the connect/create operation runs. If `createAndStore` fails, `mcp-state.json` will incorrectly indicate the server is enabled even though it didn’t connect. Move the `delete(...)` + `writeDisabledState(...)` to after a successful `createAndStore`, or wrap with a bracket/ensuring pattern to restore the ID on failure.

Missing `mcp-state.json` is an expected first-run scenario, but the current `catchCause` logs a warning for all failures (including file-not-found). This can create noisy logs in normal operation. Consider detecting the NotFound/ENOENT case and skipping (or downgrading) the warning for that specific error, while still warning on parse/permission errors.

Updates to `disabledFromPersistence` + `writeDisabledState(...)` are not synchronized. If `connect`/`disconnect` run concurrently in separate fibers, writes can race and lose updates (last-writer-wins on a snapshot of the Set). Consider serializing persistence writes (e.g., a mutex/semaphore around mutate+write, or storing IDs in an Effect Ref/SynchronizedRef and updating atomically) to avoid inconsistent `mcp-state.json`.

Persisted disabled IDs that no longer exist in config are kept indefinitely in `disabledFromPersistence` (and will be re-written on the next state change). To prevent `mcp-state.json` from accumulating stale entries over time, consider pruning the loaded Set to only include known configured MCP IDs during init (and optionally writing back the pruned set once).

This test doesn’t remove/initialize `mcp-state.json` before exercising `disconnect`. If another persistence test ran earlier (or a prior run left state behind), this can cause order-dependent behavior and make failures harder to diagnose. Add a cleanup step at the beginning of the test (remove the file, then proceed) so it is hermetic.

New Home-related translation keys were added here, but only en/zh were updated. For all other locales these strings will fall back to English (because locale dicts are merged over the base en dict). If Home v2 is intended to be localized, add these keys to the other locale dictionaries (even as temporary English copies) to avoid mixed-language UI.
The close button’s aria-label is hardcoded in English. Please use the existing localized key (e.g. language.t("common.closeTab")) so non-English locales get the correct accessible name.
